minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee failed to reach a supermajority on a write-in vote minimum and postponed choosing a chair.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the Cemetery Commission ask for control of its planned new building, which drew pushback over shared use with the DPW. Members were told to talk with the town manager and DPW director. They also reviewed town counsel's comments on defining weeks and business days, filling vacancies, and the second annual town meeting. A motion on a minimum write-in vote requirement did not reach a supermajority. A Dec 12 work session and Jan 9 public hearing were planned, and the chair election was postponed.

what_happened.line: A motion to accept the write-in minimum vote language as drafted failed to reach the supermajority needed, with two members voting no.
The committee postponed electing a chair until its next meeting.
The Cemetery Commission asked for control of its new storage building; the commissioners were told to talk with the town manager and DPW director before any charter change.
The commission described the building as self-funded, while a member asked how funding would be requested from the town.
A work session was set for December 12 and a public hearing for January 9; someone is to ask the town clerk for the current signature number behind the write-in minimum.

why_it_matters: The write-in minimum decides how many votes a write-in candidate needs to win an election, so the final wording will shape a charter question residents may be asked to vote on.
Who controls the cemetery building, and whether it shares space with the DPW, touches whether any of its cost reaches the town budget, which is mostly taxes.
watch_next: December 12, 7 p.m.: work session with votes on major items, and the postponed chair election.
January 9: public hearing on the proposed charter changes.
